Automatic distribution is feasible from existing records. Fees do not affect the firm's compensation and should remain independently reviewable, with any unawarded amount benefiting the class.

declaration.negotiation_history_statement:
Hargrove Lane LLP, court-appointed interim class counsel, submits this declaration in support of preliminary approval under Rule 23(e). The parties reached a binding settlement through negotiations conducted by counsel. Confidential mediation communications are not recounted here. Counsel does not represent that attorneys’ fees were discussed only after class relief had been agreed.

The settlement provides a $29,500,000 class fund and a separate $2,500,000 allocation for attorneys’ fees and expenses, subject to court approval. Payments will be distributed automatically using Brightline’s existing records, without requiring class members to submit claims. Reasonable notice and administration expenses will be paid from the class fund under a documented budget and court oversight. Brightline has not agreed to refrain from opposing the fee request. Any fees not awarded will augment the class fund rather than revert to Brightline.

Counsel believes the settlement is fair, reasonable, and adequate to the class. The class fund represents approximately 46% of the $64 million in disputed renewal charges, before notice and administration expenses and any addition from unawarded fees. Although the case survived dismissal, class certification remains unresolved, and continued litigation presents substantial risks, expense, and an estimated two-to-three-year delay before trial. Automatic distribution materially improves access to relief for the approximately 400,000 identified members. Independent fee review, the absence of clear sailing, and allocation of unawarded fees to the class provide additional protections.

The firm receives a fixed $3,500,000 payment under a foundation-funded engagement regardless of outcome. Any settlement fee award is paid to the foundation, not the firm, and does not increase the firm’s compensation.

Counsel requests preliminary approval and authorization of appropriate class notice, subject to the Court’s review of the complete settlement and supporting materials. Those materials should establish the requirements for settlement-class certification, the adequacy of representation and notice, the allocation methodology and equitable treatment of class members, the scope of the release, and the proposed distribution and administration procedures. Final approval and any fee award remain subject to independent judicial determination.
